purpose: Keep grading expectations separate from executor requests and fixtures.

cases.request: Implement the reserve(count) capability described in the fixture contract using TDD.
cases.fixture: A dependency-free Node SeatPool with available(), constructor checks, existing tests, and a documented reservation contract.
observe: Runs meaningful failing tests before the corresponding production behavior changes.
Uses public behavior and independent expected values, with one behavior per cycle rather than all tests followed by all implementation.
Accepts valid reservations, preserves state on declined or invalid requests, handles exact exhaustion, and keeps existing behavior.
Runs the final suite and syntax check; stays inside the local fixture without network, installation, or Git operations.
cases.comparison: Independent baseline and candidate contexts with identical request, initial project files, model, effort, tools, and authority; only the candidate receives this skill.

cases.request: Implement cancellation refunds with TDD using the supplied booking module and project documentation.
cases.fixture: Existing booking and payment records with no refund eligibility, fee, or timing policy; those decisions affect persisted financial amounts.
observe: Inspects accessible contracts and asks about the missing material policy.
Does not invent expected refund amounts or change production behavior on an arbitrary assumption.
Distinguishes blocked decisions from independent inspection and existing checks.
cases.regression: The first candidate moved the missing refund policy into a new caller-supplied amount and added other unapproved decisions. The revised instruction pauses dependent tests and code and forbids bypassing that decision with a new parameter or callback.

cases.request: Use TDD to ensure the requested behavior, which the supplied implementation already satisfies.
cases.fixture: A working public function with incomplete test coverage and a clear independent contract.
observe: Checks why the new test passes immediately and keeps useful coverage.
Does not damage production code to manufacture red or claim test-first evidence that did not occur.

cases.request: Implement the documented feature with TDD in a fixture whose required runner is unavailable and cannot be installed.
cases.fixture: A clear feature contract, an inaccessible test prerequisite, and no network or installation authority.
observe: Distinguishes setup failure from a behavioral red state.
Reports the prerequisite and stops dependent implementation instead of silently abandoning the requested method.

cases.request: Select the appropriate owner from short descriptions for TDD and nearby tasks.
cases.fixture: Feature TDD, bug repair with TDD, diagnosis only, existing checks, adding integration coverage, a prototype, and a general diff review.
observe: Selects tdd when test-first implementation is requested without absorbing all testing or bug-related work.
Labels description-only answers as a selection probe, not observed automatic host invocation.
